audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was given to Mel and 2+ items to Dr. Mundo, while whys[4] says 'At 6 it's skill-dependent' and whys[6] says 'it evens out'.
audit.why: Packet chart reads Mel, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Skill — matching the whys exactly. Win rate 56.96% over 1071 games.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and 2+ items both become Skill — ratings 3/6/6/6/5/6/5.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike was built around a 'global heal' Mel does not have, and no spike carried a cooldown.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse is a global DAMAGE strike (25000 range) that hits everyone carrying Overwhelm and scales with the number of stacks — 120/100/80s. It is not a heal, and it means denying her poke is what defuses her ult. Radiant Volley is 10/9/8/7/6s, Solar Snare 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, Rebuttal 38/35/33/29/26s.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike now describes Golden Eclipse correctly, with the stack-denial consequence spelled out.

audit.whatIsWrong: THE decisive interaction was inverted: the page said 'her Overwhelm reflect (W) does nothing to your regen'. Rebuttal reflects enemy PROJECTILES back at the attacker, and Infected Bonesaw is a projectile — so your main poke tool gets returned to your own face. Separately, Solar Snare is called her W in four places (it is her E, and W is Rebuttal), the R is called 'Rewrite Destiny' in four places (it is Golden Eclipse), and Radiant Volley is said to out-range you.
audit.why: Kit data: Mundo's Q carries the projectile flag; Mel's W reflects projectiles, blocks damage entirely and grants her move speed on a 38s rank-1 cooldown. Radiant Volley reaches 950 while Infected Bonesaw reaches 975 — Mundo out-ranges her, not the reverse. The mirror audit (mel__drmundo) already corrected exactly this reflect interaction from the other side.
audit.corrected: State that Rebuttal eats and returns your cleaver, so you bait the barrier before you poke; fix all the slot and name errors; correct the range claim.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage makes you nearly unkillable in long fights. The lane flips from 'survive' to 'walk at him' the moment you hit 6.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse (120s at rank 1) hits you anywhere on the map and scales with her Overwhelm stacks — deny the poke and you defuse it.

edits.before: You're a raid boss in side lanes and a front line in fights. The only losing move is fighting burst windows without R.
edits.after: You win the 1v1 outright, but her zone control and global R hold the game even — frontline, and make her waste Rebuttal.

edits.before: Mel's R Rewrite Destiny is a global heal, and her W Solar Snare roots you for a poke window, but neither stops a health-stacking Mundo. Your R Maximum Dosage out-sustains her whole combo and you can still all-in through the root once it ends. She has no way to burst you down — keep the pressure on.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse (R) is global — it strikes you anywhere and deals more for every Overwhelm stack she has landed, so denying her poke IS defusing her ult. Solar Snare (E, 11s at rank 1) roots you to open the burst window; your passive eats that first root and drops a canister. Keep the pressure on.

edits.before: Your HP spike buries her. A single Q slow plus E connection kills the fragile mage before Rewrite Destiny matters, and her Overwhelm reflect (W) does nothing to your regen. Roam and snowball — she's the squishiest thing in your lane pool.
edits.after: Your HP spike buries her, but Rebuttal (W, 38s at rank 1) REFLECTS projectiles — Infected Bonesaw comes straight back at you, so bait the barrier before you throw. Once it drops, one Q slow plus Blunt Force Trauma kills her. Roam and snowball.

edits.before: This is where you take over. Mel is a squishy ranged mage who pokes with Radiant Volley (Q) and stacks Overwhelm, but once you hit 3 your Q Infected Bonesaw slow lets you walk her down and E Blunt Force Trauma one-shots her tempo. Her burst can't out-damage your regen this early. Force her off the wave and deny her free stacking.
edits.after: This is where you take over. Mel pokes with Radiant Volley (Q) on a 10s cooldown at rank 1, but at 3 your Infected Bonesaw — a flat 4s and 975 range against her 950 — walks her down, and Blunt Force Trauma resets your auto on top. Her burst can't out-damage your regen yet. Force her off the wave and deny free Overwhelm stacking.

edits.before: Mel's Radiant Volley out-ranges you at level 1 and lets her free-poke and stack Overwhelm.
edits.after: Mel's Radiant Volley zones you at level 1 and free-pokes you into Overwhelm stacks.

edits.before: Level 1 tilts slightly to Mel — her Radiant Volley (Q) out-ranges you and she can free-poke your green bar and start stacking Overwhelm before you can engage. Level 2 is a skill affair; hug the wave, dodge her Q, and set up for your level-3 power spike rather than eating poke for nothing.
edits.after: Level 1 tilts slightly to Mel — Radiant Volley (Q) zones a wide area and stacks Overwhelm on you for free. Your cleaver actually reaches further, 975 to her 950, so answer from max range. Level 2 is a skill affair; hug the wave, dodge her Q, and set up your level-3 spike.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are yours. At 3 your Q Infected Bonesaw slow plus E Blunt Force Trauma auto let you walk down a squishy ranged mage whose burst can't beat your regen, and even her level-6 R Rewrite Destiny heal and W Solar Snare root can't save her from your all-in. Force her off farm and snowball.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are yours. At 3 your Infected Bonesaw slow plus Blunt Force Trauma's auto-reset walk down a mage whose burst can't beat your regen. Respect Rebuttal (W): it reflects your cleaver straight back, so throw Q only once the barrier is spent, then all-in through Solar Snare's root.

edits.before: By first item you hard-win the 1v1 — one Q-E connection deletes her — but full build the game evens out because Mel's real value is teamfight zone-control and R utility from behind a peel wall. Build MR so her magic does nothing to you, and just avoid getting caught by a W snare into her team's follow-up.
edits.after: By first item you hard-win the 1v1 — one Q-E connection deletes her — but full build evens out because Mel's real value is teamfight zone-control and global Golden Eclipse damage from behind a peel wall. Build MR, and avoid getting caught by a Solar Snare root into her team's follow-up.

edits.before: Root you with W Solar Snare to open a burst window
edits.after: Root you with E Solar Snare to open a burst window

edits.before: Scale to teamfights where R Rewrite Destiny utility matters
edits.after: Scale to teamfights where Golden Eclipse damage lands

edits.before: - Mel Solar Snare: matchup-defining — Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your engage/committal tool: never waste it on chip damage. - Your ultimate: the win condition — spend it on kill windows, not on waves.
edits.after: - Solar Snare (E, 11s at rank 1): her root — your passive eats the first one. - Rebuttal (W, 38s at rank 1): reflects projectiles, so it throws Infected Bonesaw back at you — bait it before you poke. - Golden Eclipse (R, 120s): global, scaling with every Overwhelm stack you let land.

edits.before: Track Mel's Solar Snare: Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. When it is down — Cleaver-slow + run him down.
edits.after: Rebuttal (W, 38s) reflects projectiles — your cleaver comes back at you. Bait it, then Q-slow and run her down.

edits.before: Cleaver-slow him when Solar Snare is down
edits.after: Cleaver-slow her once Rebuttal is spent

edits.before: From 6, Maximum Dosage turns extended fights unwinnable for Mel. Cleaver-slow, walk him down with E, and only disengage if his Solar Snare burst window is up and your R is down.
edits.after: From 6, Maximum Dosage turns extended fights unwinnable for Mel — but Golden Eclipse reaches you anywhere, so deny the Overwhelm stacks that power it. Cleaver-slow, walk her down, and never throw Q into an active Rebuttal.

notes: Highest-value fix here matches what the mirror (mel__drmundo) already found from her side: Rebuttal REFLECTS projectiles and Infected Bonesaw is a projectile, so Mundo's poke is returned to him. This page had it exactly backwards — 'her Overwhelm reflect (W) does nothing to your regen' — on the interaction that decides the lane. Also killed a fabricated ultimate: Mel's R was called 'Rewrite Destiny, a global heal' in four fields; it is Golden Eclipse, global DAMAGE that scales with Overwhelm stacks, which flips the advice from 'her heal doesn't matter' to 'denying poke is how you defuse her ult'. Solar Snare was labelled her W in four places — it is her E, and W is Rebuttal. And Radiant Volley does not out-range you: 950 against Infected Bonesaw's 975. Level 6 and 2+ items moved to Skill to match the packet and the whys.
